entities.summary: Per Brahe the Elder (1520–1590) was a Swedish statesman, born into a prominent noble family, and served as the Chancellor of Sweden from 1560 to 1572, playing a key role in the country's politics during the Protestant Reformation. He was instrumental in the establishment of the Swedish Riksdag, a national parliament that would shape the country's governance for centuries to come. Through his diplomatic efforts, Brahe secured significant trade agreements with European powers, fostering Sweden's economic growth and strengthening its position in the Baltic region. His legacy as a statesman and diplomat has endured, with Brahe remaining a celebrated figure in Swedish history and a testament to the country's resilience and adaptability during times of turmoil. Brahe's son, Carl Brahe, succeeded him as Chancellor, cementing the family's influence on Swedish politics. Brahe's influence extended beyond Sweden, as he played a crucial role in the establishment of the Lutheran Church in Sweden, shaping the country's religious identity. His commitment to the Protestant Reformation led to the adoption of Lutheranism as the official state church, leaving a lasting impact on Swedish society and culture. Brahe's diplomatic prowess was also evident in his efforts to secure peace treaties with neighboring countries, including the Treaty of Stettin, which marked a significant turning point in Swedish foreign policy.
